issues.legal_issue: A municipal rate assessed on land together with tenant-owned huts may be particularized to identify the portion attributable to the huts, which the landowner may recover.
material_facts: The landowner's land was assessed together with huts built and occupied by tenants who owned the huts.
The High Court directed that the assessment be particularized for each portion of land and hut, separately on the consolidated valuation.
The landowner challenged the assessment and recovery of the rate attributable to the tenants' huts.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's direction for particularizing the assessment addressed the complaint, and the landowner could collect the rate attributable to the tenant-owned huts under Section 202 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951.
issues.legal_principle: Section 202 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951 is more or less a self-contained code. What is leviable under it cannot be prejudiced by the existence of another provision. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: proceeding_is_special_leave_petition and land_is_owned_by_assessing_owner and huts_are_owned_by_tenants and assessment_combines_land_and_huts

predicates.proceeding_is_special_leave_petition: The matter is brought before the court as a petition seeking special leave to appeal.
predicates.land_is_owned_by_assessing_owner: The person assessed as owner owns the land on which the structures stand.
predicates.huts_are_owned_by_tenants: The tenants occupy huts on the land and own those huts.
predicates.assessment_combines_land_and_huts: The municipal assessment values the land and the tenant-owned huts together.

issues.definition: When the proceeding is a special leave petition, the assessed person owns the land, tenants own huts on it, and the assessment combines them, the assessment is particularized and the owner may recover the hut-attributable rate.

issues.legal_issue: A rent-control enactment does not bar a landowner from recovering municipal rates attributable to tenant-owned huts when the municipal law separately permits recovery of those rates.
material_facts: The landowner sought to recover from tenants amounts beyond the rent fixed under the Thika Tenancy Act.
The amounts at issue were municipal rates recoverable under Section 202 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951.
issues.conclusion: The Thika Tenancy Act did not prevent recovery of sums permissible under Section 202 because the former dealt with rents and the latter with rates.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished the Thika Tenancy Act, which deals with rents, from Section 202 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951, which deals with rates. The special provision governing rates prevails as to those rates. The Court cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: proceeding_is_special_leave_petition and landlord_tenant_relationship_exists and rent_is_governed_by_a_rent_control_regime and claimed_amount_is_a_municipal_rate_recoverable_from_the_tenant

predicates.proceeding_is_special_leave_petition: The matter is brought before the court as a petition seeking special leave to appeal.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_exists: A landlord leases land to tenants who occupy structures on it.
predicates.rent_is_governed_by_a_rent_control_regim: A rent-control regime governs the rent payable by the tenants.
predicates.claimed_amount_is_a_municipal_rate_recov: The claimed amount is a municipal rate that the municipal law permits the landlord to recover from the tenant.

issues.definition: When a special leave petition concerns a landlord-tenant relationship, rent governed by a rent-control regime, and a recoverable municipal rate, the landlord may recover that rate separately from the fixed rent.

issues.legal_issue: A special provision governing owners of basti properties does not violate equality when those properties form a distinct class and the owners' position is protected by the provision.
material_facts: The landowner challenged the special treatment of owners of basti properties as discriminatory under Article 14 of the Constitution.
The Court treated bastis and their dwellers as a distinct class and noted that the municipal provision protected the owners' position.
issues.conclusion: The Article 14 challenge failed because bastis and their dwellers formed a distinct class and the owners' position was protected by Section 202 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not bar special treatment of a distinct class. The Court held that bastis and their dwellers stood in a separate class and that Section 202 of the Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951 protected the owners' position. The Court cited no earlier cases.

predicates.proceeding_is_special_leave_petition: The matter is brought before the court as a petition seeking special leave to appeal.
predicates.equality_challenge_targets_special_treat: The challenger claims that special treatment of owners of basti properties is discriminatory.
predicates.basti_properties_form_a_distinct_class: The properties and their occupants are treated as a distinct social and factual class.
predicates.owners_have_a_protective_recovery_mechan: A legal mechanism protects the owners' position by permitting recovery of attributable municipal rates.

issues.definition: When a special leave petition challenges special treatment of basti owners, the properties form a distinct class, and the owners have a protective recovery mechanism, the equality challenge is rejected.
